studies.Title: Evaluation of vitamin E and selenium supplementation for the prevention of bladder cancer in SWOG coordinated SELECT.
studies.Authors: Lotan Y, Goodman PJ, Youssef RF, Svatek RS, Shariat SF, Tangen CM, Thompson IM, Klein EA
studies.Population: Men in the SELECT trial aged 50+ (black) or 55+ (all others)

sample_size.excerpt: Source documentation was obtained on 229 cases. Upon review 3 patients were excluded from analysis because they were misreported as bladder cancer, and 2 were excluded due to insufficient source documentation to confirm the diagnosis, leaving 224 bladder cancer among the 34,887 eligible, evaluable SELECT participants.( 18 ) Of the 35,533 men who were randomized 646 were excluded from all analyses, including 10 due to prior diagnosis of prostate cancer (in another the diagnosis was discovered after primary publication) and 15 who never received proper informed consent, while all 621 participants from 2 clinical sites were excluded due to severe data and participant management problems.
sample_size.location: RESULTS, paragraph 1

cases.excerpt: Table 1 lists the characteristics of the 224 men with and the 34,663 without bladder cancer.

effect_size.excerpt: The bladder cancer rate was higher in the 3 treatment arms than in the placebo arm but no difference was statistically significant (vitamin E HR 1.06, 99% CI 0.72 – 1.53, selenium HR 1.13, 99% CI 0.78–1.63, vitamin E plus selenium HR 1.05, 99% CI 0.71 – 1.51).

confidence_interval.excerpt: The bladder cancer rate was higher in the 3 treatment arms than in the placebo arm but no difference was statistically significant (vitamin E HR 1.06, 99% CI 0.72 – 1.53, selenium HR 1.13, 99% CI 0.78–1.63, vitamin E plus selenium HR 1.05, 99% CI 0.71 – 1.51).

p_value.excerpt: the 56 in the vitamin E group (HR 1.05, IRQ 0.64 – 1.73, p = 0.79)

comparison.excerpt: SELECT was designed as a 4 group trial with 5 prespecified comparisons, including selenium vs placebo, vitamin E vs placebo

design.excerpt: SELECT was a phase 3 randomized, placebo-controlled trial of selenium (200 µg daily from L -selenomethionine) and/or vitamin E

timing.excerpt: While overall cancer rate was a preplanned analysis, the bladder cancer incidence was not. However, the medical records to support this endpoint were collected in a prospective manner.

continent.excerpt: SELECT on 34,887 men from a total of 427 participating sites in the United States, Canada, and Puerto Rico

exposure_measurement.excerpt: vitamin E (400 IU daily of all- rac-α-tocopheryl acetate) and matched selenium placebo

gender.excerpt: SELECT was limited to men.
